story: S001: Define standard output structures for all hook types
story_description: Create a unified output schema that all hooks use to communicate results back to the system, including permission decisions, modified inputs, stop decisions, and system messages.
task: T004: Implement HookOutputSchema.swift with all output types
task_description: Implement the core hook output types including HookOutput struct, HookSpecificOutput, PermissionDecision enum, StopDecision enum, HookExitCode enum, and HookOutputBuilder fluent interface.
atom_description: Implement the full hook output schema with HookOutput as the main return type containing continue flag, suppressOutput flag, optional systemMessage, and hookSpecificOutput for PreToolUse/PermissionRequest hooks. Includes PermissionDecision enum (allow/deny/ask), StopDecision enum (approve/block), HookExitCode enum (success=0, blockingError=2, nonBlockingError=1), and HookOutputBuilder fluent builder pattern.
problem_statement: Hooks need a standardized way to communicate their results back to the system. Without a unified output schema, each hook would define its own return format, leading to parsing complexity, inconsistent behavior, and difficulty in adding new hook types. The output schema must support permission decisions for blocking hooks, input modification for middleware patterns, stop decisions for agent lifecycle control, and system message injection for context augmentation.
scope_in: HookOutput struct with continue, suppressOutput, systemMessage, and hookSpecificOutput fields
HookSpecificOutput struct with permissionDecision, updatedInput, decision, and reason fields
PermissionDecision enum with allow, deny, and ask cases plus displayName, icon, and color computed properties
StopDecision enum with approve and block cases plus displayName computed property
HookExitCode enum with success (0), blockingError (2), and nonBlockingError (1) cases plus description property
HookOutputBuilder fluent interface with continue_, suppressOutput, systemMessage, allow, deny, ask, updatedInput, build, and buildJSON methods
Codable and Sendable conformance for all public types
CaseIterable conformance for PermissionDecision and StopDecision enums

UI components for displaying hook outputs (separate story)
Hook output persistence or logging (separate task)
assumptions: AnyCodable type exists in the project for type-erased JSON values
JSONEncoder is available from Foundation for serialization
Swift 5.9 or later with strict concurrency support for Sendable
All hooks will return HookOutput or throw an error
Exit code 2 is reserved for blocking errors per Claude Code convention
constraints: Must conform to Codable for JSON serialization to/from CLI
Must conform to Sendable for safe use in async hook execution
PermissionDecision must match Claude Code expected values (allow/deny/ask)
Exit codes must match Claude Code documentation (0=success, 2=blocking, other=non-blocking)
HookOutputBuilder must use value semantics (copy on write) for thread safety
All string properties must be optional to support partial outputs
functional_requirements: FR1: HookOutput.continue defaults to true and controls whether hook chain processing continues
FR2: HookOutput.suppressOutput defaults to false and controls whether hook output appears in logs
FR3: HookOutput.systemMessage is optional and injects text into Claude system context when present
FR4: HookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision controls automatic approval/rejection of tool calls
FR5: HookSpecificOutput.updatedInput allows hooks to modify tool input before execution (middleware pattern)
FR6: HookSpecificOutput.decision controls whether agent stop is approved or blocked
FR7: HookSpecificOutput.reason provides human-readable explanation for decisions
FR8: PermissionDecision.allow auto-approves the action without user confirmation
FR9: PermissionDecision.deny auto-rejects the action without user confirmation
FR10: PermissionDecision.ask defers to default Claude behavior (prompt user)
FR11: PermissionDecision provides displayName, icon (SF Symbol), and color (hex) for UI rendering
FR12: StopDecision.approve allows the agent to stop normally
FR13: StopDecision.block forces the agent to continue despite stop request
FR14: HookExitCode.success (0) means stdout is shown to Claude
FR15: HookExitCode.blockingError (2) means stderr is returned and processing stops
FR16: HookExitCode.nonBlockingError (1 or other) is logged but processing continues
FR17: HookOutputBuilder.build returns the constructed HookOutput value
FR18: HookOutputBuilder.buildJSON returns pretty-printed sorted JSON string
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: All types must be Sendable for safe concurrent access in async contexts
NFR2: JSON encoding must complete in under 1ms for typical outputs
NFR3: Memory footprint must be under 1KB for typical HookOutput instances
NFR4: HookOutputBuilder must support method chaining without heap allocations
NFR5: All enum raw values must be lowercase strings for JSON compatibility

data_model_changes: New HookOutput struct: { continue: Bool, suppressOutput: Bool, systemMessage: String?, hookSpecificOutput: HookSpecificOutput? }
New HookSpecificOutput struct: { permissionDecision: PermissionDecision?, updatedInput: [String: AnyCodable]?, decision: StopDecision?, reason: String? }
New PermissionDecision enum: allow | deny | ask (String raw value)
New StopDecision enum: approve | block (String raw value)
New HookExitCode enum: success(0) | blockingError(2) | nonBlockingError(1) (Int raw value)
api_contracts: HookOutput.init() creates default output with continue=true, suppressOutput=false, no message, no specific output
HookOutputBuilder.build() returns HookOutput value type (not reference)
HookOutputBuilder.buildJSON() throws EncodingError if serialization fails
PermissionDecision.rawValue returns lowercase string matching Claude Code protocol
StopDecision.rawValue returns lowercase string matching Claude Code protocol
HookExitCode.rawValue returns integer exit code matching POSIX convention
event_contracts: HookOutput is serialized to JSON and written to stdout by hook processes
HookOutput JSON must be valid single-line or multi-line JSON object
PermissionDecision is parsed from hook stdout by HookRunner (separate component)
Exit code is read from process termination status by ProcessRunner (separate component)
ui_copy: HookExitCode.success.description returns Success - stdout is shown to Claude
HookExitCode.blockingError.description returns Blocking error - stderr returned, stops processing
HookExitCode.nonBlockingError.description returns Non-blocking error - logged but continues
edge_cases: HookOutput with nil hookSpecificOutput omits the field in JSON (not null)
HookSpecificOutput with all nil fields serializes to empty object {}
PermissionDecision.ask with no reason field is valid
StopDecision.block with no reason field is valid
HookOutputBuilder with no method calls returns default HookOutput
HookOutputBuilder.deny() called without reason parameter sets reason to nil
HookOutputBuilder.buildJSON() with non-ASCII systemMessage must use UTF-8 encoding
HookExitCode initialized with unexpected raw value (e.g., 99) returns nil
PermissionDecision initialized with unknown raw value (e.g., pause) returns nil
failure_modes: JSONEncoder throws EncodingError if AnyCodable contains non-JSON-serializable value
String(data:encoding:) returns nil if UTF-8 encoding fails (buildJSON returns {})
Process exits with code 2 but writes to stdout instead of stderr (blocking error ignored)
Hook writes invalid JSON to stdout (parsing fails, hook output discarded)
Hook writes multiple JSON objects to stdout (only first parsed, rest ignored)
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookOutputSchema.swift and remove any imports. No database migrations or state changes to revert. Dependent code will fail to compile, indicating rollback scope.
